title: Rules — Big's Backyard Ultra (official Backyard Ultra format rules)
claims: The course may be a loop or out-and-back and must be 4 miles 880 feet long, with a metric equivalent of 6.7056 kilometers.
The starting corral is measured to fit the entire starting field and stays the same size throughout the event; participants must be in the starting corral at the bell.
Each loop starts precisely one hour after the last; warnings must be given 3, 2 and 1 minutes before the start, and all competitors must start at the bell with no late starts.
Except for restroom use, a competitor may not leave the course until each loop is completed; no non-competitors, including eliminated runners, are permitted on the course.

No personal aid may be received during a loop; common aid stations are allowed; each loop must be completed within an hour to count, including the final lap; no artificial aids such as trekking poles are permitted; slower runners must allow passes.
Timing of the loops is optional for the organiser to operate.

The winner is the last person to complete a loop; all others are technically recorded as DNF; results are given as distance covered per runner; if no runner completes one more loop than everyone else, there is no winner.
The race must be open ended with no fixed cap on laps or distance.
